title: Task Manager 2.0: expanded task model (status/priority/tags/subtasks), advanced UI (filters, Kanban drag-drop, dashboard, shortcuts), and stable persistence

requirements.text: Fix backend persistence so that tasks and user profiles reliably persist across calls and canister upgrades, using stable storage for per-principal task maps and per-principal next task IDs; ensure tasks created via createTask always appear in subsequent getTasks() calls for the same authenticated principal.

quotes: Users report being unable to create tasks (tasks are not saving).

acceptanceCriteria: After calling createTask, a subsequent getTasks() from the same principal returns the created task without requiring a reload or any special ordering call.
After an upgrade, previously created tasks and saved user profiles are still present for the same principal.
If an upgrade requires state transformation, add backend/migration.mo following the conditional migration policy; if not required, do not add a migration file.

requirements.text: Upgrade the backend task data model and APIs to support Task Manager 2.0 fields per task: required dueDate, status (Open/In Progress/Completed/Archived), priority (Low/Medium/High/Urgent), tags (array of text), createdAt/updatedAt timestamps, createdBy (principal), optional assignedTo (principal, future use), and a per-user persisted ordering key for Kanban (e.g., per-status order index).
acceptanceCriteria: Backend exposes an API shape that allows the frontend to create/update tasks including: status, priority, dueDate (required), and tags.
Existing tasks (created before this change) remain readable; any missing new fields are given safe defaults during read or via migration.
All task CRUD operations remain scoped to the authenticated caller (principal-based isolation).

requirements.text: Add subtasks with backend persistence: each task supports an ordered checklist of subtasks (id, title, isCompleted). Provide APIs to add/update/delete subtasks and toggle completion, and include subtask data when fetching tasks.
acceptanceCriteria: A user can add multiple subtasks to a task, mark them complete/incomplete, edit titles, and delete subtasks; these changes persist and are returned by getTasks().
Subtask operations are authorized the same way as tasks (only the task owner principal can modify).

requirements.text: Update the task create/edit UI to match the upgraded task model: make due date a required field; add status, priority, and tags inputs; display created/updated metadata where appropriate; ensure all user-facing validation and error text is in English.
acceptanceCriteria: The task form cannot be submitted without a due date; the UI shows an English validation message for missing required fields.
The task form supports editing status, priority, and tags, and saving updates reflects immediately in the list/Kanban views.
Any backend validation failures are shown in the form without closing it (retain existing improved mutation error UX).

requirements.text: Implement due-date intelligence in the UI: show dynamic countdown badges for tasks (Today, Tomorrow, Due in X days, X days overdue, Done) and visually highlight overdue tasks (red left border + light red background) in both List and Kanban cards; ensure badge text updates correctly based on current date.
acceptanceCriteria: Tasks display the correct badge text and color based on due date and completion status, matching the requested labels (e.g., "Due today", "Tomorrow", "2 days left", "3 days overdue", "Done").
Overdue tasks that are not completed are visually highlighted in both list items and Kanban cards.
Badge logic works for tasks with due dates in the past/future and for completed tasks.

requirements.text: Expand task organization features: add advanced filtering (status including Archived, due-date ranges: Today/This Week/Overdue, priority, tags) and sorting (Due Date default, Priority, Created Date, Alphabetical) plus quick filter chips (Overdue, Due Today, High Priority, Completed).
acceptanceCriteria: Users can filter tasks by status (including Archived), due-date range (Today/This Week/Overdue), priority, and tags, and can search title/description.
Users can sort by Due Date (default), Priority, Created Date, and Alphabetical, with ascending/descending where applicable.
Quick filter chips apply and clear the corresponding filters, and the results are consistent across List and Kanban views.

requirements.text: Upgrade Kanban to support multiple columns by status (Open, In Progress, Completed, Archived as appropriate) with drag-and-drop between columns; on drop, update the task status and persist per-user ordering so the same order is restored after refresh.
acceptanceCriteria: Users can drag a task card between Kanban columns; dropping updates task status and the UI reflects the change immediately.
Within a column, users can reorder tasks via drag-and-drop and the order persists after a full page reload.
The backend stores and returns enough ordering information to restore per-user Kanban order reliably.

requirements.text: Add dashboard summary metrics for the signed-in user: open tasks count, completed today, overdue count, and tasks due this week, computed from the user’s tasks and displayed prominently on the task page.
acceptanceCriteria: The task page shows the four metrics (open, completed today, overdue, due this week) and they update when tasks are created/updated/completed.
Metric calculations treat dates consistently (use the same time unit conversions used elsewhere in the app).

requirements.text: Add modern productivity UX (UI-only where necessary): quick add / command palette, keyboard shortcuts (N new task, F search, K command palette), inline edit for common fields, duplicate task, archive/unarchive task, bulk select with bulk actions (complete, archive, delete), and lightweight notification banners for due soon/overdue.
acceptanceCriteria: Keyboard shortcuts work when the user is on the tasks page and do not interfere with typing inside form fields.
Users can select multiple tasks and apply bulk actions with clear confirmation for destructive actions.
Duplicate creates a new task with copied fields (title/description/due date/status/priority/tags) but a new id.
Archive/unarchive is supported in the UI and integrated into filters and Kanban columns as specified.
Due soon / overdue banners appear and can be dismissed for the current session.

requirements.text: Replace real-time collaboration with periodic refresh: configure task fetching to automatically refresh on an interval and on window focus, while maintaining good UX (no disruptive loading states) and ensuring React Query cache stays consistent after mutations.
acceptanceCriteria: Tasks refresh automatically on a reasonable interval and on window focus, without flashing the entire page into a loading state.
After create/update/complete/reopen/delete operations, the tasks list/Kanban remains consistent with the backend without requiring a manual reload.

requirements.text: Improve overall UX polish: add loading skeletons for task lists/Kanban, responsive layout refinements for mobile, and an optional dark mode toggle that uses the existing theme token system.
acceptanceCriteria: While tasks are loading, the UI shows skeleton components instead of empty content.
The tasks page (toolbar, list, Kanban, form) remains usable on small screens without horizontal scrolling.
A dark mode toggle exists and correctly switches styles across primary screens using the existing CSS variables/theme tokens.

requirements.text: Add a custom empty-state illustration asset and render it in the unauthenticated landing screen and/or the tasks empty state (when there are no tasks), served as a static frontend asset (do not route through the backend).
acceptanceCriteria: The generated illustration is stored in frontend/public/assets/generated and is referenced directly by the React UI.
When the task list is empty, the UI shows an empty state that includes the illustration and clear English text prompting the user to create a task.

constraints: Backend must remain a single Motoko actor with all business logic in backend/main.mo; add backend/migration.mo only if required for upgrading existing state (conditional migration policy).
Do not edit any files under frontend/src/components/ui or other frontend immutablePaths; compose existing UI components instead.
Use English for all user-facing strings added or modified by this change.
No WebSockets or third-party real-time systems; implement periodic refresh using React Query only.
Authentication must remain Internet Identity; multi-user isolation must remain principal-based.
nonGoals: Implementing Google OAuth, email/password login, forgot-password flows, or any third-party authentication provider.
Adding external databases (PostgreSQL/Prisma/Redis) or moving to Next.js/Node/Express.
True real-time collaboration or presence indicators.
Team/workspace sharing of tasks between principals (future-ready fields are acceptable, but no cross-user sharing behavior now).

required: Minimal flat-vector empty state illustration featuring a clipboard, checkmarks, and a small plant, in a green-forward palette (empty-state-clipboard.dim_1200x800.png)
